title: Hazmat Shipping 101: Compliance Essentials for Industrial and Automotive Brands
summary: Hazmat shipping compliance starts with accurate item data.
body_markdown:
Hazardous materials can show up in an[industrial or automotive supplier’s catalog](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/the-importance-of-data-analytics-in-the-automotive-aftermarket) in less obvious ways. Lithium batteries in power tools, aerosol brake cleaners, chemical coolants, and other chemical treatments can all require special handling under U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations. The work starts before a shipment reaches the warehouse, though. The classification, Safety Data Sheet (SDS), and product specifications need to be accurate in the item record first.


That makes hazmat shipping compliance a data problem before it becomes a shipping problem. When regulatory information is missing or incorrect, a supplier can run into problems during retailer item setup, electronic data interchange (EDI), and[advance ship notice (ASN)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest) processing. Those issues can delay onboarding, hold orders, and create chargebacks after an item is live.


For suppliers working with new retailers, distributors, or original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), getting this information right early can make the process much easier to manage.


## What Counts as Hazmat?


Hazardous materials aren’t limited to the products most people immediately associate with the term. Federal regulations under[49 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49) classify hazardous materials into nine hazard classes, covering everything from explosives and gases to corrosive and miscellaneous materials.


For[industrial and automotive suppliers](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/5-metrics-to-track-for-automotive-and-industrial-supply-chain-kpis) , some of the most commonly overlooked products include:


-


- **Lithium batteries:** Batteries used in power tools, diagnostic equipment, electronics, and other products can fall under Class 9, depending on their characteristics and how they’re shipped.
